overall_reason: Visitor mode inferred as Read (a dated studio article): the article names its designer and its sources by organisation, but its two survey figures (Meltwater's 54%, the Human Flourishing Lab's 77%) carry no link, year or study title; the sweep's lexicon_copy hit on 'illustrative' is the phrase 'Figma moved toward illustrative play', a description of Figma's style, not a self-label.

score.reason: T-FIGURE-AUDIT fails once for the article's unlinked survey figures (INT-011); the other figures carry a year and an attribution, and no proof is invented.

findings.where: article body, p elements in div.blog-post, 1440 (tiles/1440-03.png, tiles/1440-04.png)
findings.evidence: The article says 'Consumer sentiment research from Meltwater shows 54% negative response to recognizable AI-generated imagery' and 'The Human Flourishing Lab found that 77% of Americans use nostalgic memories as a source of comfort'. Neither gives a year, a study title or a link; the only link in the article body points to Energie.be.
findings.after: Link each study and give its year and sample
findings.why: A reader of an opinion piece relies on these figures as the evidence for its argument, and cannot check them.
findings.root: The article cites sources by name only, never by link
